**Understanding Quick Sort**

Quick Sort is a divide-and-conquer algorithm that selects a pivot element from the list to partition the other elements into two sub-arrays, according to whether they are less than or greater than the pivot. The sub-arrays are then recursively sorted.

**Worst-Case Scenario**

The worst-case scenario for Quick Sort occurs when the pivot is chosen such that it always divides the array into two sub-arrays of size 1 and n-1, where n is the size of the array. This happens when the pivot is the smallest or the largest element in the array, and the same element is chosen as the pivot in each recursive call.

**Recurrence Relation**

T(n) = T(1) + T(n-1) + O(n)

Simplifying the recurrence relation, we get:

T(n) = T(n-1) + O(n)

T(n-1) = T(n-2) + O(n-1)

T(n) = T(1) + O(n) + O(n-1) + ... + O(2)

T(n) = O(n^2)

**Code to Solve the Problem**

```python
class Node:
    def __init__(self, data):
        self.data = data
        self.next = None

def operation(head):
    p = head
    q = head.next
    r = head

    while (p.next != None):
        p = p.next

    while (q != None):
        q.next = None
        q = q.next

    while (r != None):
        r.next = p
        r = r.next

    return head
```
